newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico gov't details energy investment from Quebec.
newsitem.headline: Mexico gov't details energy investment from Quebec.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Ministry said Quebec officials plan to spend more than $250 million in various bilateral energy projects.

In a recent four-day visit to Mexico with representatives from 20 businesses, Quebec Natural Resources Minister Guy Chevrette announced a number of agreements between the governments and private companies, which the ministry detailed:
- Mexico's Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) with Hydro-Quebec International (HQI), to constuct hydroelectric generation plants.

- Gaz Metropolitain plans to spend $250 million to convert to natural gas fuel between 36,000 and 100,000 autos per year over the next five years. The company also plans to work with Mexico's national oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos to provide natural gas service stations.

- HMS-Energie, a unit of Hydro-Quebec, agreed to work with the CFE to study using "Hydrosoft River Management System" in southeast Mexico. The system is a computerized water distribution system developed only in Quebec.
- Quebec Association for Energy Efficiency and Mexico's Electric Sector Trust for Energy Savings Programs agreed to join experience and information for common projects.
The ministry said further cooperative agreements on electric transmission, public lighting and electric center sales should be reached in coming weeks.
